Kerala Police FIR against GLAS Trust over alleged forgery in BYJU’S insolvency caseNovember 2, 2026, 15:31 IST
Share
Share
Summary
Kerala Police have registered an FIR against GLAS Trust Company LLC and others over alleged forgery and cheating in BYJU'S parent company Think & Learn's insolvency proceedings. The complaint, filed at Palarivattom Police Station on October 20, 2026, alleges GLAS Trust used a forged lender-authorisation letter to claim a ₹11,432.98 crore debt and 99.41% voting share in the creditors' committee. Separately, the Kerala High Court admitted a review petition challenging GLAS Trust's authority but declined to stay the insolvency proceedings.
Key Takeaways
Kerala Police registered an FIR against GLAS Trust for alleged forgery in BYJU'S insolvency proceedings.
The complaint alleges GLAS Trust used a forged document to represent lenders and secure voting rights.
The Kerala High Court admitted a review petition challenging GLAS Trust's authority but did not stay insolvency.
The case adds to the significant legal and financial challenges facing BYJU'S and its founder.
Allegations center on a July 2024 letter, claimed to have reused signatures from an earlier January 2024 document.

Frequently Asked Questions
Q. What is the main allegation against GLAS Trust in the BYJU'S insolvency case?
A. GLAS Trust is accused of forgery and cheating by relying on a forged lender-authorisation letter to represent creditors and exercise voting rights in BYJU'S insolvency.
Q. Who filed the complaint against GLAS Trust leading to the Kerala Police FIR?
A. Rajendran Vellappalath, managing director of Voizzit Technology Private Limited, filed the complaint on October 20, 2026, at Palarivattom Police Station.
Q. What specific document is central to the forgery allegations against GLAS Trust?
A. The complaint challenges the authenticity of a Direction Letter dated July 25, 2024, which GLAS Trust allegedly used to establish its mandate from lenders.
Q. What sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita are invoked in the FIR against GLAS Trust?
A. The FIR invokes Sections 318(4), 336(3), 340(2), 61, and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, covering cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.
Q. How does the alleged forgery impact GLAS Trust's claimed voting share in BYJU'S insolvency?
A. Petitioners claim excluding disputed pages would reduce GLAS Trust's lender support from approximately 95% to around 42%, below the required 50% threshold.
Q. What is the status of the legal challenge in the Kerala High Court regarding BYJU'S insolvency?
A. The Kerala High Court admitted a review petition by Voizzit Technology on October 27, seeking reconsideration of its June 12 judgment, but declined to stay CIRP.
Q. What other significant legal challenges is Byju Raveendran currently facing?
A. Raveendran faces recovery of $1.2-billion US term loan dues, contempt charges in Singapore, and a $235-million arbitration claim by Qatar Holding.
First Principles
Corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP)
A time-bound legal mechanism under insolvency law through which a financially distressed company is restructured or liquidated under the supervision of a resolution professional and creditors. It governs the admission of claims, formation of a creditor committee, and approval of resolution plans.
Committee of creditors (CoC)
A statutory body formed during insolvency proceedings comprising financial creditors of the distressed entity, empowered to evaluate and vote on resolution plans. Voting rights within the CoC are typically proportional to the value of each creditor's admitted claim.
Voting share in committee of creditors
The proportional voting power held by a creditor within the CoC, calculated based on the size of their admitted financial claim relative to total admitted debt. A dominant voting share can effectively grant a single creditor or trustee control over resolution outcomes.
Lender-authorisation threshold
The minimum percentage of lenders by loan value required to grant a trustee or agent the legal mandate to act on their collective behalf in insolvency or restructuring proceedings. Falling below this threshold invalidates the agent's standing to vote or represent creditors.
US term loan
A fixed-duration, typically senior secured loan extended by institutional lenders, often governed under US law and used by corporates for large-scale financing. In leveraged or cross-border contexts, such loans are frequently syndicated and administered by a trustee or agent acting on behalf of the lender group.
Beneficial interest in shares
The economic entitlement to the value and returns of shares, distinct from legal ownership or registered title. Relinquishing beneficial interest is a mechanism used in settlement negotiations to transfer economic rights without necessarily changing the registered shareholder of record.

Kerala Police have registered an FIR against GLAS Trust Company LLC and several others over allegations of forgery and cheating in the insolvency proceedings of Think & Learn Private Limited, the parent company of BYJU’S.
The complaint alleges that GLAS Trust relied on a forged lender-authorisation letter to establish its right to represent creditors and exercise voting rights in the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP). The disputed document allegedly supported recognition of a claim of ₹11,432.98 crore and a 99.41% voting share in the committee of creditors (CoC).

The FIR was registered at Palarivattom Police Station in Ernakulam City on October 20, 2026, following a complaint by Rajendran Vellappalath, managing director of Voizzit Technology Private Limited. The case invokes Sections 318(4), 336(3), 340(2), 61 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, covering alleged cheating, forgery, use of a forged document and criminal conspiracy.
ADVERTISEMENT
Allegations centre on July 2024 letter
The complaint challenges the authenticity of a Direction Letter dated July 25, 2024, which GLAS Trust allegedly relied upon to establish its mandate to act on behalf of lenders.
According to the petitioners’ bench note filed in a review petition before the Kerala High Court, the letter was allegedly assembled using signature pages from an earlier Direction Letter dated January 18, 2024. The petitioners claim that the dates on 12 pages were changed to July 25, 2024, even though the signatures were taken from the earlier document.

The petitioners have also alleged that signature images were reused across additional pages and that the document was created in Word and subsequently converted into a PDF, rather than being executed through electronic signatures.
The alleged alterations are significant because the petitioners dispute whether GLAS Trust had the requisite lender backing to act on their behalf. Their bench note states that authorisation from lenders holding more than 50% of the loan was required. They claim that excluding the disputed pages would reduce the lender support cited by GLAS from approximately 95% to around 42%, below the required threshold.

High Court admits review petition
The police case comes amid a separate legal challenge before the Kerala High Court. On October 27, the court reportedly admitted a review petition filed by Voizzit Technology Private Limited and Voizzit Information Technology LLC, seeking reconsideration of its June 12 judgment in the BYJU’S insolvency matter. However, it declined to stay the ongoing CIRP of Think & Learn.
ADVERTISEMENT
The review petition seeks a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation, Enforcement Directorate and National Investigation Agency into alleged irregularities in the insolvency proceedings. The petitioners have relied on what they describe as fresh electronic evidence concerning the July 2024 lender-authorisation letter, as per reports.
The latest development adds to the legal and financial challenges facing Byju Raveendran and the BYJU’S group. Creditors are pursuing recovery of dues linked to a $1.2-billion US term loan, while Raveendran is also facing legal proceedings in India and overseas.
ADVERTISEMENT
Think & Learn was admitted to insolvency proceedings in July 2024 over unpaid sponsorship dues of ₹158.9 crore to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) subsequently approved a settlement and closed the proceedings. However, the Supreme Court set aside that order in October 2024 following a challenge by GLAS Trust.
Separately, a Singapore court sentenced Raveendran to six months in prison in May 2026 in a contempt case involving alleged non-compliance with asset disclosure orders. More recently, he proposed relinquishing his beneficial interest in 17.89 million shares of Aakash Educational Services as part of a proposed settlement relating to a $235-million arbitration claim by Qatar Holding.
